relevantSteps.title: Start the rice
relevantSteps.detail: Rinse 300 g Japanese short-grain rice. Add to a saucepan with the water amount directed on the rice packet, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for about 12–15 minutes or as the packet directs. Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff.

relevantSteps.title: Make the regional sauce base
relevantSteps.detail: Heat 1 tbsp neutral cooking oil in the pan over medium-low heat; do not let it smoke. Add 15 g garlic, 15 g fresh ginger, finely minced, grated or sliced as appropriate. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without burning. Pour in 120 ml vegetable stock and stir, scraping the base of the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in 2 tbsp soy sauce only after liquid is present. Dissolve over low heat for 1–2 minutes, stirring; keep sweet or salty condiments away from a dry, very hot pan. Take off the heat and cover the base briefly while cooking the main; leave the delicate finishing ingredients for the final sauce step.

relevantSteps.title: Finish the regional sauce
relevantSteps.detail: With the cooked main and side ready, gently warm the separate sauce base if needed.  Once the sauce base is ready, take the pan off the heat. Loosen 1.5 tbsp white miso, 1 tbsp yuzu kosho with a spoonful of the warm cooked sauce, then stir it all back in. Keep this sauce gentle rather than bringing it back to a hard boil, to retain the delicate aroma. Off the heat, add 1 tbsp rice vinegar gradually. Fold through the cooked sauce and taste before adding extra seasoning. Off the heat, stir in or scatter over 1 tsp shichimi togarashi, 0.25 tsp sansho pepper, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds. Off the heat, fold in 15 g spring onion, 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil. Wash and finely chop the fresh produce first. Add the toasted sesame oil only as a finishing seasoning, not as frying oil. Finish and plate immediately so the fresh seasoning stays bright.

relevantSteps.title: Start the rice
relevantSteps.detail: Rinse 300 g Basmati rice. Add to a saucepan with the water amount directed on the rice packet, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for about 12–15 minutes or as the packet directs. Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff.

relevantSteps.title: Make the regional sauce base
relevantSteps.detail: Heat 1 tbsp neutral cooking oil in the pan over medium-low heat; do not let it smoke. Add 15 g garlic, finely minced, grated or sliced as appropriate. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without burning. Lower the heat. Stir in 1.5 tsp advieh, 0.5 tsp freshly ground black pepper for 15–20 seconds just until fragrant, then add the liquid promptly so the ground spices do not scorch. Pour in 120 ml vegetable stock and stir, scraping the base of the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Spoon a little of the hot cooking liquid into a cup and soak 0.1 g saffron threads in it for 5 minutes. Return all the saffron and borrowed liquid to the pan; this uses the liquid already listed, not a second portion. Add 2 dried limes. Pierce the dried limes. Infuse at a gentle simmer for at least 5 minutes, leaving them in during the main's simmer when applicable. Take off the heat and cover the base briefly while cooking the main; leave the delicate finishing ingredients for the final sauce step.

relevantSteps.title: Finish the regional sauce
relevantSteps.detail: With the cooked main and side ready, gently warm the separate sauce base if needed. After the sauce has simmered, lift out and discard the woody pieces of dried limes before the final garnishes; do not eat these whole aromatic pieces. Off the heat, add 15 ml lemon juice gradually. Fold through the cooked sauce and taste before adding extra seasoning. Off the heat, fold in 15 g fresh mint. Wash and finely chop the fresh produce first. Finish and plate immediately so the fresh seasoning stays bright.

relevantSteps.title: Cook the sorghum
relevantSteps.detail: Rinse 840 g whole sorghum grain. Bring 6000 ml water to a boil in a roomy saucepan, add the grain and simmer uncovered for about 50–60 minutes, or the packet's longer time, until chewy-tender with no hard centre. Keep submerged with boiling water as needed, then drain thoroughly. Spread in a shallow dish to lose excess steam briefly before dressing.

relevantSteps.title: Make the regional sauce base
relevantSteps.detail: Heat 3 tbsp neutral cooking oil in the pan over medium-low heat; do not let it smoke. Add 45 g garlic, finely minced, grated or sliced as appropriate. Stir for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without burning. Lower the heat. Stir in 1.5 tsp freshly ground black pepper for 15–20 seconds just until fragrant, then add the liquid promptly so the ground spices do not scorch. Pour in 360 ml vegetable stock and stir, scraping the base of the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add 6 bay leaves. Leave the whole aromatic pieces intact so they can be lifted out. Infuse at a gentle simmer for at least 5 minutes, leaving them in during the main's simmer when applicable. Stir in 3 tsp dried thyme, 4.5 tsp dried oregano. Simmer gently in the liquid for 2–3 minutes, stirring until evenly dispersed. Take off the heat and cover the base briefly while cooking the main; leave the delicate finishing ingredients for the final sauce step.

relevantSteps.title: Finish the regional sauce
relevantSteps.detail: With the cooked main and side ready, gently warm the separate sauce base if needed. After the sauce has simmered, lift out and discard the woody pieces of bay leaves before the final garnishes; do not eat these whole aromatic pieces. Off the heat, add 90 ml lemon juice gradually. Fold through the cooked sauce and taste before adding extra seasoning. Off the heat, fold in 45 g flat-leaf parsley. Wash and finely chop the fresh produce first. Finish and plate immediately so the fresh seasoning stays bright.

relevantSteps.title: Cook the grain
relevantSteps.detail: Rinse 280 g brown rice. Add to 2000 ml boiling water and simmer for 25–40 minutes, or the packet's time, until tender with no hard centre. Top up boiling water to keep submerged, then drain well. Start the kale during the grain's final 10 minutes.

relevantSteps.title: Wilt the kale
relevantSteps.detail: Start these side-finishing actions about 8 minutes before serving, overlapping the main's final cooking or rest. For a main that cooks faster than this, begin these actions before starting the main. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat, add 250 g thinly sliced kale leaves and 30 ml water. Cover briefly, then stir for 6–8 minutes until tender; add a spoonful of water if needed. Take off the heat and finish with 20 ml lemon juice. Serve cooked grains and noodles promptly, or keep them at 60°C or hotter while waiting; keep cold garnishes chilled until assembly. For advance preparation, divide into shallow containers and refrigerate as soon as they stop steaming, at 5°C or colder. Do not leave a pot of rice cooling on the bench. Reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

relevantSteps.title: Finish the regional sauce
relevantSteps.detail: Finish when the main has reached its endpoint and the side is ready.  Off the heat, add 30 ml lemon juice gradually. Fold through the cooked sauce and taste before adding extra seasoning. Off the heat, fold in 15 g fresh basil. Wash and finely chop the fresh produce first. Finish and plate immediately so the fresh seasoning stays bright.
